summary: The main article describes a photocatalytic synthesis of tetra-substituted furans promoted by CO2, featuring optimization tables, substrate scope schemes, and mechanistic investigations. The document includes 1 table for reaction optimization and 5 schemes detailing synthetic approaches, substrate scope, and the proposed reaction mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Approaches to access highly substituted furans via : (a) successive direct functionalization of furan C -H; (b) condensation; (c) annulation of unsaturated substrates with ketones or imines; (d) migratory cycloisomerization and rearrangements.
items.description: This scheme summarizes four classical and modern literature approaches for the synthesis of highly substituted furan rings.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: CO2-promoted organic transformations: (a) rearrangement of propargyl alcohols to unsaturated ketones; (b) cross-coupling using native allylic alcohol; (c) oxidation of allylic alcohols to unsaturated aldehydes. This work: (d) synthesis of tetra-substituted furans.
items.description: This scheme compares previous CO2-promoted reactions with the current work's photocatalytic synthesis of tetra-substituted furans.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Control experiments for the reaction of 1a
items.description: This table presents control experiments demonstrating the necessity of CO2, light, photocatalyst, and base for the formation of furan products 1b and 1c.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Substrate scope of tetra-substituted furan from 1,3-diketone.
items.description: This scheme illustrates the variety of 1,3-diketones and 3-oxo-esters that can be converted into substituted furans and dihydrofurans under the optimized conditions.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Mechanistic studies.
items.description: This scheme details experimental results from radical trapping with TEMPO and in situ NMR studies to support the proposed mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Proposed reaction mechanism.
items.description: This scheme outlines the full catalytic cycle involving single electron transfer, CO2 adduct formation, and acylcyclopropane rearrangement.
